subject.title: [security] AWS, Azure, and GCP lease release deletes provider resources without ownership read-back

question: Should AWS, Azure, and GCP managed lease release fail closed unless a live provider read-back proves the resource is the exact Crabbox-owned lease resource before deletion?
rationale: The source-supported issue sits on a documented destructive provider security boundary, but the fail-closed behavior can change cleanup and recovery outcomes for stale or drifted resources, so maintainers should own the security/compatibility choice before implementation.

options.title: Fix fail-closed release ownership
options.body: Require live provider ownership and matching lease identity before AWS, Azure, and GCP release deletion, preserving cleanup errors when proof is missing.

options.title: Scope by provider first
options.body: Land provider-specific fixes or waivers if Azure companion-resource identity or AWS/GCP proof needs separate review units.

options.title: Accept coordinator-state authority
options.body: Keep deleting from stored cloudID/name without live read-back, accepting a weaker boundary than VISION.md and SECURITY.md describe.

recommendation.title: Fix fail-closed release ownership
recommendation.body: Require live provider ownership and matching lease identity before AWS, Azure, and GCP release deletion, preserving cleanup errors when proof is missing.
